purpose: Test whether the topology-changing OR3 -> OR2+XOR3 carrier reopens the simplest holographic/Pfaffian route. Prove a stronger local obstruction: no invertible common 2x2 basis can make even OR2 and XOR3 simultaneously satisfy the necessary matchgate parity condition. Equality fanout is not needed for the contradiction.

setup.constraint_signatures: OR2 has values [0,1,1,1] on 00,01,10,11. XOR3 is the odd-parity indicator on three bits.
setup.basis: Let T=[[A,B],[C,D]] be an arbitrary invertible characteristic-zero 2x2 transform on constraint legs. A common holographic basis would use the dual transform on variable/equality legs.
setup.necessary_matchgate_condition: Every matchgate signature has support on only one Hamming parity. Therefore transformed OR2 and transformed XOR3 must each be pure even or pure odd parity.

theorem.name: NO_COMMON_INVERTIBLE_BASIS_MAKES_OR2_AND_XOR3_BOTH_MATCHGATE_PARITY

OR2_odd: Odd parity for OR2 requires o0=o2=0, so B is 0 or -2A and D is 0 or -2C.
Invertibility eliminates the (B,D)=(0,0) and (-2A,-2C) choices. The two surviving forms are B=0,D=-2C with A,C nonzero, or B=-2A,D=0 with A,C nonzero.
For B=0,D=-2C, XOR3 has x1=-2A^2 C and x2=-4AC^2, both nonzero. For B=-2A,D=0, XOR3 has nonzero coefficients on both parities as well. Thus XOR3 cannot be pure parity.
OR2_even_XOR3_even: Even OR2 gives AD+BC+BD=0. Invertibility forces B,D nonzero in the XOR-even subcase.
XOR-even requires x3=0, hence D^2=-3C^2, and x1=0.
Using A=-B(C+D)/D from the OR2 equation, x1=-B^2(C^2-2D^2)/D. Therefore C^2=2D^2.
Combining C^2=2D^2 with D^2=-3C^2 gives 7C^2=0, impossible in characteristic zero together with D nonzero.
OR2_even_XOR3_odd: Even OR2 again gives AD+BC+BD=0. Invertibility forces B,D nonzero in the XOR-odd subcase.
XOR-odd requires x0=0, hence B^2=-3A^2, and x2=0.
Using C=-D(A+B)/B from the OR2 equation, x2=-D^2(A^2-2B^2)/B. Therefore A^2=2B^2.
Combining A^2=2B^2 with B^2=-3A^2 gives 7A^2=0, impossible in characteristic zero together with B nonzero.

theorem.corollary: No one-common-basis holographic transform can turn the v4.1 topology-changed OR2+XOR3 constraint network into a local matchgate/Pfaffian network. This remains true before imposing any EQ3/EQd variable-fanout conditions.

killed: Use the v4.1 OR2+XOR3 decomposition and then apply one common invertible 2x2 holographic basis to make all constraint nodes matchgates.
Any claim that replacing OR3 by parity-friendly XOR3 alone evades the earlier common-basis obstruction.
not_killed: Independent edge-dependent gauges whose transformations cancel along each network edge.
Topology-changing gadgets with additional polynomial auxiliary structure beyond the v4.1 two-bit gadget.
A genuinely nonlocal Pfaffian/determinant contraction not decomposed into local parity signatures.
